subject: Media Literacy
title: Bandwagon Effect
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Bandwagon Effect.

hook.text: 'Everyone is switching to our product!' You feel the pull — even if you don't need the product.

buildup.text: The bandwagon effect exploits our instinct to follow the crowd. If everyone's doing it, it must be right.

discovery.text: Social proof is hardwired into human psychology — it helped our ancestors survive.

twist.text: Propagandists fabricate social proof. Fake polls, paid crowds, and bot armies create the illusion of consensus.

climax.text: The bandwagon doesn't tell you where it's going. Just that everyone's on it.

punchline.text: Popular doesn't mean correct. It means popular.

quiz.question: How do propagandists exploit the bandwagon effect?
options: By fabricating social proof through fake polls, crowds, and bots
